points.t: A **tender, growing, crusted or keratotic nodule** or non-healing ulcer on the face, lip, ear, scalp, hands or a chronic wound.
**Cumulative UV**, immunosuppression (transplant), HPV, chronic wounds and scars; arises from **AK or Bowen’s**.
**Suspected cancer pathway** (NG12 1.7.4); surgical excision first-line; check nodes; transplant patients need specialist surveillance.
**Lip and ear SCC** (higher metastatic risk), SCC in a chronic ulcer or scar, rapid KA-like growth, immunosuppressed patients.

cause.lead: UV damage climbs a ladder from AK to invasive SCC.
points: Second commonest skin cancer; metastasis overall ~2–5% (lip ~10–15% in older series).
Risks: outdoor work, older age, fair skin; **transplant recipients 65–250×**; CLL, HIV.
Drugs: azathioprine, **voriconazole**, **hydrochlorothiazide**, BRAF inhibitors.
Chronic wounds / burns (**Marjolin ulcer**), radiation, arsenic, smoking (lip), lichen sclerosus / planus.
UV-signature **TP53** mutations → AK / Bowen’s → invasive SCC.

visuals.caption: Squamous cell carcinoma: a keratotic, ulcerated nodule with hard everted edges, as tumour strands invade down into the dermis.
visuals.alt: Skin cross-section with ulcerated nodule and invading tumour strands

features.lead: Tender, hard, growing over weeks to months.
points: Indurated **tender** keratotic nodule or plaque, or **ulcer with hard everted edges**; often bleeds.
Sites: scalp, ears, **lower lip**, backs of hands, lower legs in women.
**Lip SCC**: lower vermilion on **actinic cheilitis**; persistent ulcer / crust, induration; smokers.
Variants: cutaneous horn, verrucous / carcinoma cuniculatum (plantar), KA-type, poorly differentiated.
**AK / Bowen’s turning into SCC**: induration, tenderness, rapid growth, bleeding, ulceration, > 1 cm, treatment failure.

visuals.caption: High-risk sites (coral): ear and lower lip. Common sun-exposed sites (teal) include scalp, temple and backs of hands; always palpate the pre-auricular, parotid and neck nodes.
visuals.alt: Head profile marking ear and lip sites and neck nodes

items.name: Marjolin ulcer
items.t: SCC in a chronic leg ulcer.

points: Pre-auricular, parotid, cervical, submental / submandibular (lip).
Excision preferred; else incisional / punch deep enough for depth.
Differentiation, depth, perineural / lymphovascular invasion, margins; BAD 2020 risk group.
Specialist: node ultrasound ± FNA; CT / MRI for very high-risk.

cards.name: Keratoacanthoma
cards.clue: Rapid crateriform nodule; treat as SCC.

cards.name: Merkel cell carcinoma
cards.clue: Rapid red-violet nodule in the elderly.

manage.lead: Recognise and refer; surgery is specialist.

points: **NG12 1.7.4**: suspected cancer pathway (2 weeks); refer **within 1 working day**.
**Lip or oral ulcer > 3 weeks**: head-and-neck / oral pathway or urgent dental.
Peripheral margins: **low risk 4 mm; high risk 6 mm; very high risk 10 mm** (± adjuvant radiotherapy, MDT).
Advanced: **cemiplimab** (TA802).
High-risk features: lip / ear / scar site, > 20 mm, > 4 mm thick, poor differentiation, perineural / LVI, recurrence, immunosuppression.
AK field therapy: 5-FU, diclofenac 3%, imiquimod, tirbanibulin.
Bowen’s: topical **5-FU 5%** after confirmed diagnosis within a documented plan.
Review **hydrochlorothiazide** (MHRA) and long-term **voriconazole**; transplant photoprotection; smoking cessation; SPF lip balm.
Transplant: joint care (mTOR switch, acitretin); nicotinamide is specialist-only.

limits.t: Freeze, curette or treat suspected SCC in primary care unless accredited.
Never together (fatal DPD inhibition); keep 5-FU off eyes / mucosa.

items.t: Lip or mouth ulcer > 3 weeks: head-and-neck pathway.
New growth or non-healing area in a long-standing ulcer or scar: biopsy (Marjolin).

pearls.t: **Tender + hard + growing** turns an AK or Bowen’s into suspected SCC.
Teach patients to report a lump in the scar or neck.
Mark lesions on a body map.

quiz.q: Which sites carry higher metastatic risk?
quiz.a: Lip and ear (and scars / chronic wounds).
Suspected cancer pathway (NG12 1.7.4), within 1 working day.

quiz.q: Excision margin for a low-risk SCC?
quiz.a: 4 mm (high risk 6 mm, very high risk 10 mm).

quiz.q: Drug never to combine with topical 5-FU?
